title: Introduce staged tenant-scoped backup/restore with rollforward hooks
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: On large private deployments customers asked for safer, tenant-scoped upgrade and rollback tooling that minimizes blast radius and supports partial rollforward when a single tenant needs a schema correction. This PR introduces a staged backup residency model, tenant-scoped snapshot tagging, a 'dry-apply' schema migration runner, and a pluggable rollforward hook system so operators can apply fixes to a single tenant without a full cluster rollback.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new backup residency controller to the installer operator. Backups are now marked as 'staged' and optionally kept in a short-term residency store to enable rapid partial restores.
- Adds tenant-scoped snapshot tagging (annotations on S3/GCS/MinIO objects + Terraform state tags) so snapshots can be discovered and restored per-tenant.
- Implements a dry-run path for SQL schema migrations that records the proposed DDL/DDL-order without changing production state. Dry-runs are stored alongside snapshots.
- Introduces rollforward hooks: a lifecycle hook type operators can write to run corrective statements or replay logic against a single-tenant snapshot after restore. Hooks are namespaced per-tenant and executed in a sandboxed transaction by default.
- Helm chart and Terraform updates to expose residency TTL, snapshot retention policies, and enable per-tenant annotations during install/upgrade.

Checklist: 
- [x] Backup residency controller + CRD and controller unit tests
- [x] Snapshot tagging + Terraform state patch and tests
- [x] Dry-run migration runner and storage format compatibility tests
- [x] Rollforward hook API + executor and e2e test harness
- [x] Helm chart values and example override for on-prem installs
- [x] Documentation draft included in installer README and examples

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-2314, ENG-2387, PM-402

Testing notes: 
- Unit test coverage added for controller reconcile paths and minio adapter.
- Integration job in CI spins up a local MinIO + Postgres and runs an end-to-end tenant restore + rollforward using the example playbook. The e2e runs are marked as long and gated behind the 'e2e-long' job.

CI status: Initial run: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, e2e-long: fail (flaky network in MinIO container); rerun: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, e2e-long: pass. Lint warnings addressed in follow-up commit.

Deployment/upgrade notes: The stagedbackup CRD is opt-in by default; existing installs will not change behavior unless residency is enabled via helm values or Terraform parameter. There is a migration path that converts existing snapshot archives to tagged snapshots using a migration job (included). Operators should plan for a short maintenance window when enabling residency for the first time for large archives.

Security considerations: Rollforward hooks execute SQL against tenant schemas. Hooks run in a sandboxed transaction and are limited by role-based DB access granted by the operator. The hook executor also signs manifests to avoid replay attacks. See docs section for recommended RBAC and KMS key policies.

Why this is different from prior work: Existing PRs added generic backup/restore and rollback guards; this PR focuses on minimizing blast radius by enabling tenant-level restores, keeping short-term staged snapshots for rapid recovery, and providing a controlled rollforward mechanism so fixes can be applied without cluster-wide downgrades or full rewinds.

Notes for reviewer: The residency store interface is intentionally minimal so it can be implemented for different object stores; prefer reviewing the interface contract and the minio adapter unit tests first. The dry-run migration format must be compatible with our eval tooling; double-check the JSON manifest schema in installer/migrations/dryrunner/record_writer.go.

discussion_thread:
Reviewer: Diego Morales: 'Would prefer the default TTL to be conservative (7d) and require explicit override for shorter retention; otherwise we risk S3 costs.'
Author: Aisha Patel: 'Agreed; default TTL set to 7d in values.yaml. We added helm chart comment to call out cost tradeoffs.'
Reviewer: Claire Hsu: 'Can we ensure rollforward hooks never run outside a transaction? We shouldn't allow partial commits.'
Author: Aisha Patel: 'Hook executor now wraps hooks in a sandboxed transaction; added unit test to validate rollback on error.'
Reviewer: Jonah Klein: 'Dry-run format looks good but ensure compat with eval harness schema v2.'
Author: Aisha Patel: 'Updated record_writer to include schemaVersion and added conversion helper.
